note: Unified Twig Extensions auto-loads PHP-defined Twig functions/filters/tags from the DEFAULT theme's `<theme>/*/_twig-components/{functions,filters,tags}/` folders (glob is one level below the theme). functions/*.php must set $function (a \Twig\TwigFunction); filters/*.php must set $filter (a \Twig\TwigFilter); tags/NAME.tag.php must define class Project_NAME_TokenParser. Files starting with '.', '_' or 'pl_' are skipped. Only service is newcity_twig.twig_extension (class ExtensionAdapter, tag twig.extension). No config, permissions, Drush, plugins, or configure route. Medium cases stage a namespaced custom theme `ute_twig` with a known function/filter file for the agent to READ (non-invasive: theme not installed/defaulted). Hard cases require the agent to CREATE a working extension file; verify transiently installs ute_twig, makes it default, renders it via Twig, then always restores default=olivero.

evals.prompt: I enabled the unified_twig_ext module. Where does it look for custom Twig functions/filters/tags to load, and does it scan every theme or just one?
evals.expected_output: It scans only the site's DEFAULT theme (system.theme:default): it globs one directory level below the theme for `_twig-components/` folders (e.g. <theme>/source/_twig-components/) and loads PHP files from their functions/, filters/, and tags/ subfolders. Non-default themes are ignored.

evals.prompt: Using unified_twig_ext, how do I add a custom Twig function (say `greeting()`) from my theme? What must the PHP file define and where does it go?
evals.expected_output: Put a PHP file in <default_theme>/*/_twig-components/functions/ (e.g. greeting.function.php) that sets $function = new \Twig\TwigFunction('greeting', fn() => 'hello'); then run drush cr. The loader includes the file and registers $function with Twig. (Filters set $filter; tags define class Project_NAME_TokenParser.)

evals.prompt: In unified_twig_ext, which files in a _twig-components folder are skipped by the loader, and what is the Twig extension service the module registers?
evals.expected_output: Files whose base name starts with '.', '_' or 'pl_' are skipped. The module registers one service newcity_twig.twig_extension (class Drupal\unified_twig_ext\TwigExtension\ExtensionAdapter) tagged twig.extension, which loads the extensions via ExtensionLoader.

evals.prompt: On this site there is a custom theme named ute_twig that ships a unified_twig_ext-style Twig function file. Inspect that theme's _twig-components folder and tell me the machine name of the Twig function it registers.
evals.expected_output: The file web/themes/custom/ute_twig/source/_twig-components/functions/ute_known.function.php sets $function to a \Twig\TwigFunction named 'ute_known_fn'.

evals.prompt: The custom theme ute_twig on this site contains a unified_twig_ext Twig filter file. Inspect the theme and state the machine name of the Twig filter it registers.
evals.expected_output: The file web/themes/custom/ute_twig/source/_twig-components/filters/ute_known.filter.php sets $filter to a \Twig\TwigFilter named 'ute_known_filter'.

evals.prompt: The custom theme ute_twig on this site is set up to use unified_twig_ext. Add a Twig function named `ute_greeting` (following unified_twig_ext's file convention) that returns the string 'ute-hello-world', so that a Twig template rendered with the ute_twig theme can call {{ ute_greeting() }}.
evals.expected_output: Create web/themes/custom/ute_twig/source/_twig-components/functions/ute_greeting.function.php setting $function = new \Twig\TwigFunction('ute_greeting', fn() => 'ute-hello-world'); (drush cr). Rendering {{ ute_greeting() }} with ute_twig as the default theme then outputs 'ute-hello-world'.

evals.prompt: In the ute_twig theme on this site, add a Twig filter named `ute_shout` via unified_twig_ext's file convention. It must upper-case its input and append an exclamation mark, so that {{ 'hi'|ute_shout }} renders 'HI!'.
evals.expected_output: Create web/themes/custom/ute_twig/source/_twig-components/filters/ute_shout.filter.php setting $filter = new \Twig\TwigFilter('ute_shout', fn($s) => strtoupper($s).'!'); (drush cr). Rendering {{ 'hi'|ute_shout }} with ute_twig as the default theme then outputs 'HI!'.
